subject: Entitlement translation for multi-cloud bundle (AWS + GCP) — next steps
messages:
From: Nora Chen <nora@lumina-works.com>
To: jordan_blake@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 15:32:00 -0000
Subject: Mapping marketplace entitlements for our bundled offer

Hi Jordan,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We have a joint bundle we want to list: Lumina's analytics + Redwood inference runtime packaged as a single SKU in both AWS and GCP marketplaces. The partner onboarding team asked for an entitlement matrix that explains how a single SKU maps to purchaser entitlements across both clouds (VM quotas, privateLink vs VPC options, meterable units, and co-sell eligibility).

I attached a first-pass matrix (entitlement_matrix_v1.xlsx) and a short PDF showing how we call Redwood's dedicated capacity from our installer (proof_of_integration.pdf). Can we align on the translation rules? We specifically need:
- Which Redwood SKUs or entitlement signals should map to AWS metering dimensions vs GCP usage reports
- Guidance on recommended SKU names/tags so marketplace listings don't create entitlement collisions
- Any required sign-off path for co-sell tagging on the AWS side

Proposed timeline: answer questions by Friday so our PM can submit the listing package early next week.

Best,
Nora
Head of Partnerships, Lumina Works

From: jordan_blake@redwood.com
To: Nora Chen <nora@lumina-works.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 16:08:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Mapping marketplace entitlements for our bundled offer

Nora — thanks for the files, they look helpful. Short reply while I pull internal folks in who own SKU mapping and metering:

- Ben, Kim — Lumina is proposing a bundled SKU that should appear as a single purchase on AWS and GCP but deliver two logical entitlements (Lumina feature set + Redwood inference reserved capacity). They need guidance on how our metering and entitlement signals translate into marketplace metering dimensions and how to avoid duplicate consumption billing.
- Requested deliverables from our side: a single-page translation guide (examples: recommended SKUs/tags, metering dimension mapping, preferred listing metadata) and a quick checklist of what AWS/GCP will require for co-sell & private offering.

Nora — can you confirm whether the bundle will use a private offer on AWS or the public listing with a private-offer overlay? That changes the steps for co-sell tagging.

I'll get you a draft translation guide by Thursday EOD.

— Jordan
Director, Partner GTM
Redwood Inference

From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: jordan_blake@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 09:14:00 -0000
Subject: RE: Mapping marketplace entitlements for our bundled offer

Adding the technical and billing detail here after reviewing Nora's attachments. High level notes:

1) Metering model
- For AWS: prefer using a single custom metering dimension for the bundle (eg. lumina_redwood_bundle_hours) which the partner ticks. Internally we map that to Redwood reserved tokens/hour usage for billing reconciliation.
- For GCP: GCP's listing can use a usage-based SKU with a reporting metric; map to our internal metering label (redwood_reserved_unit). Avoid using both clouds' native compute metrics — that creates mismatches.

2) Entitlement signals
- Use metadata tags on the purchase (metadata key: partner_bundle, value: lumina-redwood-v1). That tag flows into both clouds and makes downstream license checks deterministic.
- Within our runtime, emit a prefix header (X-Redwood-Entitlement: bundle:lumina-redwood-v1) during handshake so Lumina can correlate calls to marketplace purchases.

3) Co-sell tagging
- AWS requires a co-sell entitlement flag during private-offer creation and a named contact in the seller portal; we'll need the AWS Marketplace PM (Cc'd) to confirm the precise contact flow.

4) Docs and deliverables
- I'll draft the translation table (example rows: purchase tag -> marketplace dimension -> internal label) and a condensed checklist for listing submission.

Action items:
- Kim: can you validate whether the tag names conflict with existing catalog entries?
- Marissa: capture any marketing language constraints for the SKU name so we don't block the copy during listing.

Ben
Head of Partnerships Ops

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: ben_carter@redwood.com, jordan_blake@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -0000
Subject: RE: Mapping marketplace entitlements for our bundled offer

Quick check from catalog: the proposed tag "lumina-redwood-v1" doesn't collide with active SKUs, but a few legacy private-offer SKUs use the "lumina-*" prefix from a historical pilot — recommend using "lumina_labs_redwood_v1" to be safe (underscore preferred for portal parsing).

Also flagged two downstream asks for the partner:
- Disclosure: marketplace listing needs a short line on data residency for inference — Lumina should confirm region behavior when Redwood dedicated capacity is used.
- Billing reconciliation: we need partners to include a monthly metering export (CSV) for the first three months to validate mapping before automated reconciliation.

I can fold these into Ben's translation table and Marissa can confirm marketing copy.

Kim
Catalog & Marketplace Ops

From: jordan_blake@redwood.com
To: Nora Chen <nora@lumina-works.com>, Liam O'Sullivan <liam@cloudbridge.io>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, AWS Marketplace PM <aws-marketplace@amazon.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 21:08:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Mapping marketplace entitlements for our bundled offer

Nora / Liam — thanks, all. Attached is a short draft we can use for the listing team (link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2bExampleSharedDoc). Highlights:
- Recommended marketplace tag: lumina_labs_redwood_v1 (per Kim).
- Metering mapping examples for AWS and GCP (see table in Drive).
- Co-sell note: AWS PM, can you confirm whether the private-offer creation form needs our seller contact or Lumina's legal contact to trigger co-sell eligibility?

Next steps:
1) Lumina confirms private-offer vs public-listing by EOD Monday.
2) Lumina provides the short data residency sentence and agrees to monthly metering export for three months.
3) We (Redwood) will prepare the final translation table and checklist and post the Drive doc; after Lumina confirms we can hand this to AWS/GCP listing teams.

I'll keep this as the canonical thread. If you prefer, we can open a quick 30-minute call next week to walk the listing PMs through the table.

Thanks — Jordan
Director, Partner GTM
Redwood Inference

Attachments: entitlement_matrix_v1.xlsx, proof_of_integration.pdf
